title: Customer Signal Orchestrator & Release Commit Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Build a disciplined, auditable orchestration layer that converts customer escalation signals (top-account SLA breaches, executive escalations, enterprise security requests) into prioritized roadmap commitments or emergency remedies with clear SLAs and release gating. Scope includes: 1) a triage scoring model for incoming signals, 2) a routing/owner assignment matrix by signal type and severity, 3) a Release Commit Protocol (RCP) to gate changes onto the public roadmap or emergency hotfix lanes, and 4) a lightweight dashboard for stakeholders to view signal status and commit decisions. Non-goals: not building a full-blown CRM integration in this phase (we will rely on webhook payloads and CSV ingest), not replacing existing exec escalation playbooks. Rationale: Recent incidents where premium accounts requested immediate behavior fixes highlighted lack of a repeatable "commit vs short-term workaround" decision flow. This project reduces ambiguity and improves SLA transparency for top accounts while keeping engineering work scoped and prioritized.
acceptance_criteria: A triage scoring algorithm is implemented that ingests signal attributes (account_tier, severity, upstream_impact, reproducibility) and produces a consistent priority score
Routing matrix exists and is enforceable: signals auto-assign to an owner (PM/Eng/SE) based on rules and shows reassignment history
Release Commit Protocol (RCP) document published and surfaced in Console: includes criteria for roadmap commit vs hotfix, required sign-offs, and commit SLA windows
Stakeholder dashboard prototype is accessible and shows live signals with status, owner, score, and decision timestamp
2 documented playbook runs (one simulated and one live) where an escalated top-account request is either committed to a release or moved to a hotfix lane and all steps recorded
decision_log: 2025-02-12: Decided to use a deterministic scoring model (weighted attributes) rather than ML in phase 1 to keep auditability and debuggability (decision by PM+Eng)

2025-02-25: Chose to implement webhook ingest with CSV fallback instead of building two-way CRM sync to accelerate MVP rollout

implementation_notes: Use deterministic weighted scoring: attributes and weights configurable via Console feature flag
Persist signal history and decision audit trail for 12 months to support customer inquiries and account reviews
Expose an API endpoint for CS/AE to trigger 'escalation simulation' to validate whether a particular signal would meet RCP commit thresholds
Dashboard will be a read-only page in Console for initial MVP with export to CSV for exec reporting
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Over-committing to roadmap due to noisy signals -> Mitigation: conservative score thresholds and requirement for PM+Eng sign-off
Risk: Regulatory/legal escalation requires more review time -> Mitigation: surface regulatory flag early in triage and include Security/Legal in auto-assigned approval chain
Risk: Duplicate signals from multiple channels causing churn -> Mitigation: implement dedupe heuristics on account+signature and show merged history
